ego.name: Zaha Hadid
ego.summary: Zaha Hadid was an Iraqi-British architect, artist, and designer who used painting and drawing to develop buildings with fractured planes, flowing lines, and changing spatial sequences. She founded Zaha Hadid Architects in London and completed cultural, civic, and sporting projects around the world.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid's father was an Iraqi industrialist, economist, and political figure. She grew up in his upper-class Baghdad household.
connections.notes: He was also known as Muhammad al-Hajj Husayn Hadid.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid's mother was an artist from Mosul. She raised Hadid in Baghdad with Mohammed Hadid.
Hadid's brother was a writer, accountant, and expert on Arab affairs. He suggested that she design the Middle East Centre building at St Antony's College, Oxford.
connections.notes: Foulath suggested that Hadid design the Middle East Centre building.

connections.relationship_description: Koolhaas taught Hadid at the Architectural Association School of Architecture. After her graduation, she worked with him at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture and remained a professional peer.
connections.notes: Koolhaas described her at graduation as "a planet in her own orbit."

connections.relationship_description: Zenghelis taught Hadid at the Architectural Association School of Architecture. After 1977, they worked together at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture in Rotterdam.
connections.notes: He called Hadid the most outstanding student he had taught.

connections.relationship_description: As Vitra's president-director general, Fehlbaum invited Hadid to design the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, completed in 1993.
connections.notes: The Fire Station became the launching point of her built architectural career.

connections.relationship_description: Schumacher began working with Hadid in 1988, became a partner at Zaha Hadid Architects in 2002, and collaborated on many of the practice's major projects.
connections.notes: Hadid described him as an enormous support and an incredible asset.

connections.relationship_description: Tschumi was among Hadid's teachers while she studied architecture at the Architectural Association School of Architecture after moving to London in 1972.
The structural engineer met Hadid through her association with Koolhaas and supported and encouraged her during the early stage of her architectural career.
Johnson co-curated the Museum of Modern Art's 1988 Deconstructivism in Architecture exhibition. Hadid was one of its seven featured architects.
connections.notes: The exhibition associated Hadid's work with deconstructivism.

connections.relationship_description: Wigley co-curated the Museum of Modern Art's 1988 Deconstructivism in Architecture exhibition. Hadid's drawings and projects were included in the show.
Hadid and British architectural artist Brian Clarke developed a proposal for the Spittelau Viaducts Housing Project in Vienna. Clarke planned glass artworks for the project.
connections.notes: The completed project did not include Clarke's proposed artwork.

connections.relationship_description: Eli Broad and his wife Edythe funded the Eli and Edythe Broad Art Museum at Michigan State University. Hadid designed the museum, which opened in 2012.
Doronin commissioned Hadid to design Capital Hill Residence in Barvikha near Moscow. Her practice completed the residence in 2018 after her death.
connections.notes: The project was completed posthumously by her practice.

connections.relationship_description: Obrist conducted and published an extended interview with Hadid as part of his Conversation Series of interviews with cultural figures.
connections.notes: Obrist published an extended interview with Hadid in his Conversation Series.

category_summaries.summary: Hadid grew up in an upper-class Baghdad family. Her father combined industry with political work, and her mother was an artist from Mosul. Her brother Foulath later suggested that she design the Middle East Centre at St Antony's College, Oxford.

At London's Architectural Association, Hadid studied with Rem Koolhaas, Elia Zenghelis, and Bernard Tschumi. Koolhaas and Zenghelis hired her at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture after graduation. Structural engineer Peter Rice encouraged her during the early years of her career.

Professional relationships brought Hadid's work before new audiences and into built commissions. Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley included her work in the 1988 Museum of Modern Art exhibition. Rolf Fehlbaum commissioned the Vitra Fire Station, and later collaborators and clients supported projects by Zaha Hadid Architects.
